parallel.requirements: Recognized the full transform math, game replay, artifact, determinism, and reference-hash workflow described in the prompt.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Despite swarm mode being enabled, the run used the main agent as the sole implementation and verification owner with no child delegation.
parallel.implementation: Implemented all eight requirement areas: Vector3, Matrix, Quaternion, Point conversion, replay I/O, replay runner, quaternion system, and simulation world.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Produced non-empty per-requirement patch files, materialized the required output tree, and left final hashes matching the reference value.
parallel.verification: Ran build, focused unit probes, full replay output generation, and official pytest acceptance; all visible checks and the session tail passed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished task obligation is visible in the completed official outcome, but actual parallel execution was not used.

serial.requirements: Received the same full task and later received harness progress updates naming quaternion_system and sim_world as still remaining.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Ran as a serial control with Agent and AgentSwarm disabled; the same main agent owned all implementation attempts across three rounds.
serial.implementation: Completed engine math, Point, replay I/O, and replay runner patch files, but did not complete quaternion_system or sim_world patch artifacts.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Built and produced the required output files, but the final state came from an incomplete game-side implementation and had the wrong reference hash.
serial.verification: Official pytest showed six visible checks passed while the same-seed replay reference-hash assertion and pytest session tail failed.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out after three rounds with two known requirement slugs absent and a stable but reference-mismatching final state hash.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel-labeled run recognized the full bootstrap task and by closure had patch artifacts for all eight required slugs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run received the same task and, by its third round prompt, was explicitly told only six of eight requirements were covered with quaternion_system and sim_world remaining.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both knew the same task, but parallel reached full requirement coverage while serial closed with two known requirements still unimplemented.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Swarm mode was available, but protocol validation shows the parallel run made zero swarm calls, direct agent calls, or subagents; the main agent owned the work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control disabled Agent and AgentSwarm tools and also made zero delegation calls across its rounds.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no true decomposition difference in coordination structure; both were single-agent attempts, but the parallel-labeled main agent completed more work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: No child briefs or cross-agent handoffs existed; integration knowledge stayed in the main trajectory, which produced game-side quaternion and simulation patches.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: No child briefs or handoffs existed in serial either; its third prompt still carried a harness update naming the missing game-side requirements.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The relevant interface gap is ordinary unfinished implementation rather than a lost or malformed cross-agent context transfer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel committed Vector3, Matrix, Quaternion, Point, replay I/O, replay runner, quaternion system, and simulation world changes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial committed Vector3, Matrix, Quaternion, Point, replay I/O, and replay runner changes, but no quaternion_system or sim_world commits appear before closure.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The missing game-side quaternion-system and simulation-world work explains why serial could build and run yet produce the wrong final state.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The main parallel-labeled turn completed normally after producing patches, output artifacts, and final hashes.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial third round ended cancelled/aborted after the final timeout window, with no child result lifecycle involved.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel reached ordinary main-agent completion; serial stopped at process timeout before finishing the remaining implementation scope.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The final parallel workspace contained all eight requirement patches and output hashes matching the expected value.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The final serial workspace contained only six requirement patches and produced a stable but incorrect final state hash.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no shared-state race; the material difference is that serial never integrated the remaining game-side behavior needed for the reference state.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel official pytest acceptance passed all seven visible checks plus the session tail.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial passed six visible checks but failed the same-seed replay reference-hash assertion and the session tail.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verified both determinism and reference-state integrity; serial verified internal same-seed equality but not the hidden reference hash.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed in one non-delegating round in about 2489 seconds and the official evaluation passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial consumed three non-delegating rounds, about 7301 seconds and 322 LLM requests, and still ended with agent_timeout plus failed evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The serial run spent much more budget but closed incomplete; this is a serial productivity and timeout gap, not parallel fan-out or child-budget exhaustion.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official parallel_only_pass outcome is explained by ordinary completion differences, not by executed parallel coordination. The parallel-labeled run never spawned child work, but it finished all eight requirement patches, generated matching final hashes, and passed official pytest. The serial run also did not delegate, consumed three timeout-limited rounds, left quaternion_system and sim_world without patch artifacts, and failed the hidden reference hash assertion after producing a different final state hash.

serial_contributors: Timed out across three serial rounds before finishing the remaining quaternion_system and sim_world requirements.
Delivered a stable same-seed replay hash that differed from the hidden reference hash.
Used no delegation, so its failure is not a parallel coordination failure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial omitted two game-side implementation requirements that parallel completed.
Serial generated a deterministic but incorrect final game state hash while parallel matched the expected hash.
